subject: Re: Privacy assessment — ownership boundary, subprocessors & evidence pack
messages:
From: Sara Mueller <sara.mueller@healthgrid.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Intake <legal@healthgrid.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Initial PAQ and evidence request — PII handling and subprocessors

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this on. HealthGrid is finishing a privacy review ahead of our procurement committee next week and we have a short Privacy Assessment Questionnaire (PAQ) focused on PII handling, data classification, and cross-border subprocessors.

Two asks to start:
- Can you confirm the ownership boundary for PII in Redwood inference (what components are in-scope vs out-of-scope for the DPA Annex)?
- Please provide:
  * current subprocessor roster (CSV) with region and function,
  * a dataflow diagram showing where PII enters/exits our environment and any shared caches, and
  * a short note on key management (who holds encryption keys for persisted telemetry).

We attached our PAQ (short) and timeline: procurement needs an evidence pack by 2026-12-06. Is that feasible? If not, tell us what you can deliver and when.

Best,
Sara Mueller
Vendor Risk Manager — HealthGrid
[Attachment: HealthGrid_PAQ_v1.docx]
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mueller <sara.mueller@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T11:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Initial PAQ and evidence request — PII handling and subprocessors

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear ask and the PAQ. We're on it. Quick response to your bullets and a delivery plan below.

Ownership boundary (high level):
- In-scope: Redwood inference control plane for model routing and customer-configured inference runtime when using Hosted API and Dedicated shared pools. This includes request routing, prefix/KV cache components, and telemetry we persist for billing/ops tied to tokens.
- Out-of-scope: customer-managed VPC private deployments (Private mode where the customer hosts the runtime), and any customer-side post-processing inside customer infrastructure.

What we will provide by 2026-12-05 EOD (US-Pacific):
1) Subprocessor roster (CSV) with region, function, and whether access to unredacted PII is possible.
2) Dataflow diagram (PDF) v3 that annotates PII ingress points, transient caches, telemetry redaction points, and egress paths.
3) Short KMS note describing key custody for persisted telemetry and for customer-managed Private deployments.
4) A DPA Annex redline (docx) showing our proposed transfer mechanism language (SCCs + standard contractual wording) and where we require onshore subprocessors for restricted data classes.

Two clarifying questions so we map evidence correctly:
- Do you need per-region segregation (EU vs US) in the roster, or is a single roster with region field sufficient?
- For the PAQ item about "ability to export raw logs containing identifiers," do you want an architectural description or a sample export artifact?

I'll upload the artifacts to a shared folder and send a DocuSign-ready DPA Annex redline for comments.

Markus Klein
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: request_ack.txt]
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T08:34:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Re: Initial PAQ and evidence request — internal alignment on DPA Annex

Markus — forwarding my notes after a quick sync with Legal. For the thread record:

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03T08:15:00-08:00

Short internal summary:
- Legal prefers: maintain SCCs + updated Annex describing transfer mechanics; avoid bespoke encryption language that implies we hold customer keys for Hosted/Dedicated.
- Ask: where we reference "onshore subprocessors" we should list only roles (e.g., "inference telemetry processing") not vendor names in the Annex; vendor names remain in the roster CSV.
- Action: Markus to provide the Annex redline and a short Q&A that maps PAQ questions to DPA clauses (so HealthGrid's legal can cross-check quickly).

I'll stand by to help match items to the PAQ.

Jordan Blake
Director, Legal Ops — Redwood Inference
From: Sara Mueller <sara.mueller@healthgrid.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Intake <legal@healthgrid.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Privacy assessment — added KMS and export questions

Thanks Markus — that timeline is helpful. A couple follow-ups attached in our updated PAQ (PAQ_v2). Highlights:
- KMS: please confirm whether telemetry persisted for billing is encrypted with a customer-specific key or a Redwood-managed key. If customer key, what KMS integrations are supported?
- Exports: we need a sample minimal export manifest (JSON/Text) that shows what fields are included when a customer requests a raw logs export — you can redact values but keep keys and types.
- Subprocessors: for any subprocessor outside the EU, note whether we have data transfer safeguards (SCCs, adequacy, or specific onshore fallbacks).

Attached: PAQ_v2 (docx). If you can send the roster and diagram first, we can start our internal mapping and follow with the Annex redline.

Cheers,
Sara
[Attachment: HealthGrid_PAQ_v2.docx]
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mueller <sara.mueller@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T16:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Privacy assessment — ownership boundary, roster & evidence pack (deliverables)

Sara — attaching the evidence pack we discussed. Thanks for the clear timeline; we prioritized the items most commonly requested by procurement/legal teams.

Deliverables (attached/uploaded):
- subprocessor_roster.csv — columns: vendor_name, function, region, access_level (none/transient/unredacted), contract_link
- dataflow_diagram_v3.pdf — single-page diagram annotated with PII ingress points, transient caches (KV cache), telemetry retention tiers, and export boundaries
- sample_export_manifest.txt — shows field keys/types for raw log exports (values redacted)
- kms_note.txt — short description of key custody: Hosted/Dedicated: Redwood-managed KMS with per-tenant key derivation; Private: customer-managed keys in their KMS/HSM (we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and on-prem HSM connectors)
- dpa_annex_redline.docx — proposed redline with SCC references and proposed clause for onshore subprocessors per restricted data classes

Summary answers to your specific follow-ups: 
- Per-region roster: we included a region column (EU/US/APAC) — that should meet your needs.
- Export manifest: attached sample_export_manifest.txt; it includes identifiers (hashed where required), timestamps, request metadata, and token counts.
- Keys: by default Hosted/Dedicated use Redwood-managed keys; if you require customer keys for telemetry, we can scope that under Private deployments or via an enterprise addendum (requires extra work and a separate KMS integration project).

Next steps:
- Please confirm if the CSV format works for your vendor intake system (we can produce JSON if you prefer).
- Jordan — can you confirm Legal is comfortable with the Annex language (I highlighted the onshore fallback paragraph for quick review)?

Thanks — happy to join a 30-min walkthrough with HealthGrid legal next week if helpful.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Privacy & Compliance, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: subprocessor_roster.csv, dataflow_diagram_v3.pdf, sample_export_manifest.txt, kms_note.txt, dpa_annex_redline.docx]
